findings.diagnosis: The prompt systematically underestimates contradiction risk when a cut leaves a prefix that reads like an independent assertion because it ends on a finite/reporting verb or other predicate‑like material without its resolving complement, so high‑contra cuts are ranked too high.
findings.evidence: ['de_de_296','de_de_1032','de_de_1009','de_de_1529','de_de_1108','de_de_1000','de_de_480']: each policy kept a cut that leaves an unresolved/assertive prefix (finite or reporting verb, or clause needing a final verb) and that cut has a high measured contra which zeroed the H_set.

edit.text: If a cut leaves a prefix that, taken alone, asserts a proposition because it ends on a finite or reporting verb (or other predicate‑like token) without its complement, ask: 'Could the remainder reverse/negate/complete this claim?' If yes, assign a near‑maximal contra.
